newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Seven killed in attacks in Tajikistan.
newsitem.headline: Seven killed in attacks in Tajikistan.

text.p: Gunmen have killed seven people, including a Russian serviceman and two ethnic Russians employed by the U.S. embassy, in a spate of attacks in the Tajik capital Dushanbe, a government official said on Wednesday.

An interior ministry spokesman said an ethnic Russian had succumbed on Wednesday morning to gunshot wounds. Six other people had already died as a result of the attacks on Tuesday night in various residential areas in the west of the city.
The attacks were the latest to rock the Central Asian state which remains tense after a four-year civil war and where dozens of Russian servicemen and civilians have been killed or wounded this year.
"We view all the killings as part of one outrageous act of terrorism," the ministry spokesman said.

The latest killings occurred one day after a two-week hostage crisis ended in the release by a rebel group of its Western and Russian hostages but highlighted the instability of Tajikistan, which borders China and Afghanistan.

The spokesman said the seven killed in Tuesday's attacks included a 46-year-old lieutenant-colonel serving with Russian border troops deployed in Tajikistan, which Moscow regards as a bulwark against Islamic fundamentalism on its southern flank.
About 20,000 Russians serve as peacekeepers in Tajikistan and guard the frontier with Afghanistan.
Two security workers from the U.S. embassy in Dushanbe, described as ethnic Russians, were also among the victims, the spokesman said.
A policeman was also killed in an attack on a psychiatric hospital he was guarding. The attackers freed one of the patients, Nazhmetdin Alimov, who belonged to a group fighting the government.
No one has claimed responsibility for the recent attacks but they have been widely blamed on Islamist opposition fighters who fought the former Soviet republic's secular government in the civil war.
A ceasefire agreed at the end of last year seems to be generally holding but isolated attacks by rogue rebel groups have continue
